## Today's questions {#roadmap data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

- Which plot matches the question and the variables?
- How do we build and annotate it in base R?
- How does ggplot2 express the same choices?

**Case study** · What changes in a vitamin C dose-response plot when we show the delivery method?

## R graphics packages {#packages data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

| Tool | Typical use |
|:---|:---|
| Base R graphics | Quick plots and direct control over drawing |
| grid | Graphics building blocks for packages such as lattice and ggplot2 |
| lattice | Trellis plots for comparisons across groups |
| ggplot2 | Layered figures with consistent scales and panels |
| plotly | Interactive figures with hover, zoom and pan |

::: {.slide-callout}
Base graphics ships with R. Today we use base graphics first, then ggplot2.
:::

## Plot choice by question {#plot-choices data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

| Question | Variables | Plot |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Where do most length measurements fall? | One numeric variable | Histogram |
| How many animals got each dose? | Categories and counts | Bar chart |
| Does length vary with dose? | Two numeric variables | Scatterplot |
| Does length differ by delivery method? | Numeric outcome and groups | Boxplot |
| How does mean length change across doses? | Ordered doses and group means | Line plot |
| How do group summaries vary across two factors? | Two groups and a summary | Heatmap |

## Starting and adding to a base plot {#base-high-low data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

| High-level calls start a plot | Low-level calls add to it |
|:---|:---|
| `plot()`, `hist()`, `boxplot()`, `barplot()` | `points()`, `lines()`, `abline()` |
| Set up axes and plotting coordinates | `text()`, `legend()`, `axis()`, `title()` |

Run the high-level call first. A later high-level call starts the next plot or panel.

## Base R histogram {#base-histogram .plot-example data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Each bar counts measurements in an interval. Bin width changes what patterns you can see.

```{r}
#| label: base-histogram
#| fig-alt: "Histogram of odontoblast length in five-unit intervals."
growth <- ToothGrowth
hist(growth$len,
     breaks = seq(0, 35, by = 5),
     xlab = "Odontoblast length",
     main = "",
     col = "#56B4E9", border = "white")
```

## Base R bar chart {#base-bars .plot-example data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Treat each tested dose as a category. The bars show how many animals received it.

```{r}
#| label: base-bars
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart showing 20 animals at each of the three doses."
barplot(table(growth$dose),
        xlab = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
        ylab = "Animals", col = "#56B4E9")
```

## Base R scatterplot {#base-scatter .plot-example data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Each point is one animal. There are only three x positions, and some points overlap.

```{r}
#| label: base-scatter
#| fig-alt: "Odontoblast lengths plotted at the three vitamin C doses."
plot(len ~ dose, data = growth,
     xlab = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
     ylab = "Odontoblast length",
     pch = 16, col = "#0072B2")
```

## Adding points and a legend {#base-overlay .plot-example .wide-code data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Start an empty plot with `type = "n"`. Draw one group at a time, then explain the symbols.

```{r}
#| label: base-overlay
#| fig-alt: "Dose response scatterplot distinguishing orange juice and ascorbic acid by color and shape."
plot(len ~ dose, data = growth, type = "n",
     xlab = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
     ylab = "Odontoblast length")
with(subset(growth, supp == "OJ"),
     points(dose, len, pch = 16, col = "#0072B2"))
with(subset(growth, supp == "VC"),
     points(dose, len, pch = 17, col = "#D55E00"))
legend("bottomright",
       c("Orange juice", "Ascorbic acid"),
       pch = c(16, 17),
       col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00"),
       bty = "n")
```

## Base R boxplot {#base-boxplot .plot-example data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

The middle line is the median. The box shows the middle half. Each box is one dose and delivery method.

```{r}
#| label: base-boxplot
#| fig-alt: "Six boxplots for orange juice and ascorbic acid at each dose."
boxplot(len ~ supp + dose, data = growth,
        xlab = "Method and dose (mg/day)",
        ylab = "Odontoblast length",
        col = c("#A6D7ED", "#F4BA9B"))
```

## Base R line plot {#base-line .plot-example data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Connect the mean lengths at the three ordered doses for the orange juice group.

```{r}
#| label: base-line
#| fig-alt: "Mean odontoblast length at three vitamin C doses for the orange juice group."
oj <- growth[growth$supp == "OJ", ]
oj_means <- aggregate(len ~ dose, data = oj,
                      FUN = mean)
plot(len ~ dose, data = oj_means, type = "b",
     xlab = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
     ylab = "Mean odontoblast length",
     pch = 16, col = "#0072B2")
```

## Base R graphics settings {#base-par data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

`par("mar")` reads a setting. `par(mfrow = c(1, 2))` changes the active device's layout for subsequent plots.

| Setting | Controls |
|:---|:---|
| `mfrow`, `mar` | Panel rows and columns, margins (bottom, left, top, right) |
| `pch`, `col`, `cex` | Point symbol, colour, relative size |
| `lty`, `lwd` | Line type and width |
| `las`, `cex.axis`, `cex.lab` | Axis tick-label orientation, tick text and axis title size |

Set labels and limits on a plot with `xlab`, `ylab`, `xlim` and `ylim`.

## Base R panels with a common scale {#base-panels .plot-example .wide-code data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Save the settings, draw both panels with the same y limits, then restore the settings.

```{r}
#| label: base-panels
#| fig-show: hold
#| fig-alt: "Side-by-side boxplots by dose for each delivery method, with identical vertical scales."
old <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1), las = 1)
for (method in c("OJ", "VC")) {
  group <- subset(growth, supp == method)
  boxplot(len ~ dose, data = group,
          main = method, ylim = range(growth$len),
          xlab = "Dose (mg/day)", ylab = "Length")
}
par(old)
```

## Saving base R plots {#base-save data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Use `png()` to open a file for drawing. Run your plotting commands again, then use `dev.off()` to finish writing the file.

```{r}
#| eval: false
png("dose-response-base.png",
    width = 7, height = 4, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(len ~ dose, data = growth,
     xlab = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
     ylab = "Odontoblast length",
     pch = 16, col = "#0072B2")
dev.off()
```

Use `pdf()` to save a figure that stays sharp when scaled.

## Reading the dose response {#base-check data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

- Which plot best shows whether the delivery methods differ at each dose?
- At which dose do the two groups look most alike?
- What can a histogram hide when we pool all the animals?

## ggplot2 {#ggplot2-intro data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

A plotting package built around the **layered grammar of graphics**.

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("ggplot2")  # Once per R installation
```

```{r}
#| message: false
library(ggplot2)
```

[ggplot2 function reference](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/)

## What “grammar of graphics” means {#grammar data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

A chart combines reusable parts.

| Part | Our dose-response scatterplot |
|:---|:---|
| Data | One row per ibservation: one animal |
| Mapping (`aes()`) | Dose on x, length on y, method sets colour and shape |
| Stat | None here; a histogram would count rows in bins |
| Geometry (`geom_point()`) | Draw each animal as a point |
| Scale and coordinates | Translate values to colours and positions |
| Facets and theme | Split into panels if useful, then style the display |

## The same scatterplot in ggplot2 {#gg-scatter .plot-example .wide-code data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Start with the data and mappings, then add points.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### ggplot2

```{r}
#| label: gg-scatter
#| fig-height: 4.15
#| fig-alt: "ggplot2 dose response scatterplot with delivery method mapped to color and shape."
p <- ggplot(growth,
            aes(x = dose, y = len)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = supp,
                 shape = supp),
             size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
       y = "Odontoblast length",
       colour = "Method", shape = "Method")
p
```

### Base R

```{r compare-base-overlay, ref.label="base-overlay"}
#| fig-height: 4.15
#| fig-alt: "Base R dose response scatterplot with colour and shape indicating delivery method."
```

:::

## Aesthetics and constants {#gg-aes data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

**Map a column** inside `aes()`. `aes(colour = supp)` assigns colours by method and creates a guide.

**Set a constant** outside `aes()`. `colour = "steelblue"` gives every point the same colour.

Other aesthetics include `x`, `y`, `shape`, `fill`, `size`, `alpha` and `linetype`. Use `group` to tell a line layer which points belong together.

## Grouping repeated samples {#gg-group data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg" .smaller}

* Indometh: 6 people, 11 samples each; 1 row is 1 sample
* Both panels show the same indomethacin measurements

```{r}
#| label: group-data
#| include: true
profile <- ggplot(Indometh, aes(x = time, y = conc)) +
  labs(x = "Time since dose (hours)", y = "Plasma concentration (mcg/mL)")
```

:::: {.group-comparison}
::: {}
**One line through all samples**

```{r}
#| label: group-unmapped
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-alt: "A single zigzag line connects measurements across different subjects at the same sampling times."
profile + geom_line()
```
:::

::: {}
**One line per subject**

```{r}
#| label: group-subject
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-alt: "Six separate lines each follow one subject's plasma concentration over time."
profile + geom_line(aes(group = Subject))
```
:::
::::

## Geometries and summaries {#gg-geoms data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

A geom controls what gets drawn.

```{r}
#| label: geom-icons
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.1
#| fig-alt: "Six small plots show the marks made by geom_point, geom_line, geom_bar, geom_histogram, geom_boxplot and geom_tile."
icon_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 18) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.margin = margin(8, 18, 14, 18))

icons <- list(
  "geom_point()" = ggplot(growth, aes(dose, len)) +
    geom_point(colour = "#0072B2"),
  "geom_line()" = profile + geom_line(aes(group = Subject),
                                     colour = "#0072B2"),
  "geom_bar()" = ggplot(growth, aes(factor(dose))) +
    geom_bar(fill = "#0072B2", width = 0.72),
  "geom_histogram()" = ggplot(growth, aes(len)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "#0072B2", colour = "white"),
  "geom_boxplot()" = ggplot(growth, aes(supp, len)) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "#A6D7ED"),
  "geom_tile()" = ggplot(aggregate(len ~ supp + dose, growth, mean),
                         aes(supp, factor(dose), fill = len)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") + guides(fill = "none")
)

grid::grid.newpage()
grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = grid::grid.layout(2, 3)))
for (i in seq_along(icons)) {
  print(icons[[i]] + icon_theme + labs(title = names(icons)[i]),
        vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = (i - 1) %/% 3 + 1,
                            layout.pos.col = (i - 1) %% 3 + 1))
}
grid::popViewport()
```

`geom_bar()` counts rows. Use `geom_col()` when you already have the bar heights.

## Histogram bins in ggplot2 {#gg-hist .plot-example data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

The histogram layer counts observations. Match the bin boundaries before comparing to the base plot.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### ggplot2

```{r}
#| label: gg-hist
#| fig-height: 4.15
#| fig-alt: "Histogram of odontoblast length with five-unit bins in ggplot2."
ggplot(growth, aes(x = len)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5,
                 boundary = 0,
                 fill = "#56B4E9",
                 colour = "white") +
  labs(x = "Odontoblast length",
       y = "Animals")
```

### Base R

```{r compare-base-histogram, ref.label="base-histogram"}
#| fig-height: 4.15
#| fig-alt: "Base R histogram of odontoblast length with five-unit bins."
```

:::

## Bar charts in ggplot2 {#gg-bars .plot-example data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Treat dose as a category. `geom_bar()` counts the animals at each dose.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### ggplot2

```{r}
#| label: gg-bars
#| fig-height: 4.15
#| fig-alt: "Three bars show 20 animals at each tested vitamin C dose."
ggplot(growth, aes(x = factor(dose))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#56B4E9") +
  labs(x = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
       y = "Animals")
```

### Base R

```{r compare-base-bars, ref.label="base-bars"}
#| fig-height: 4.15
#| fig-alt: "Base R bar chart showing 20 animals at each tested vitamin C dose."
```

:::

## Grouped boxplots in ggplot2 {#gg-box .plot-example .wide-code data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Make dose a factor to give the three tested doses their own categories. Map delivery method to the fill.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### ggplot2

```{r}
#| label: gg-box
#| fig-height: 4.15
#| fig-alt: "Grouped boxplots by dose and delivery method."
ggplot(growth, aes(x = factor(dose), y = len,
                   fill = supp)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)",
       y = "Odontoblast length", fill = "Method")
```

### Base R

```{r compare-base-boxplot, ref.label="base-boxplot"}
#| fig-height: 4.15
#| fig-alt: "Base R boxplots for each dose and delivery method."
```

:::

## Heatmap of group means {#gg-heat .plot-example .wide-code data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Reduce to one row per tile first. A tile shows the mean for a group and hides variation within it.

```{r}
#| label: gg-heat
#| fig-alt: "Heatmap showing the mean odontoblast length for the six dose and method groups."
means <- aggregate(len ~ supp + dose,
                   data = growth, FUN = mean)
ggplot(means, aes(x = supp, y = factor(dose),
                  fill = len)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_label(aes(label = round(len, 1)), fill = "white") +
  labs(x = "Delivery method", y = "Dose (mg/day)",
       fill = "Mean length")
```

## Facets share a scale {#gg-facets .plot-example data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Compare methods within each dose on a shared y scale.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### ggplot2

```{r}
#| label: gg-facets
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 2.65
#| fig-alt: "Three panels compare orange juice and ascorbic acid at each vitamin C dose. All panels use the same y scale."
ggplot(growth, aes(x = supp, y = len)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#A6D7ED") +
  facet_wrap(~ dose, nrow = 1, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(x = "Delivery method", y = "Odontoblast length")
```

### Base R

```{r}
#| label: compare-base-panels
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 2.55
#| fig-show: hold
#| fig-alt: "Base R boxplots compare the two delivery methods in three dose panels with the same y limits."
old <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4.2, 4, 2, 1))
for (amount in sort(unique(growth$dose))) {
  boxplot(len ~ supp, data = subset(growth, dose == amount),
          main = paste(amount, "mg/day"), ylim = range(growth$len),
          xlab = "Delivery method", ylab = "Odontoblast length")
}
par(old)
```

:::

## Scales, axes and guides {#gg-scales .plot-example .wide-code data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

* Scale can be changed for each Aesthetic with corresponding `scale_...`
  * A mapping says which variable controls colour.
  * The scale chooses the colours and sets the legend labels.


```{r}
#| label: gg-scales
#| fig-alt: "Scatterplot with ticks at the tested doses and a legend spelling out the delivery methods."
method_labels <- c("Orange juice",
                   "Ascorbic acid")
p_scaled <- p +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0.5, 1, 2)) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(OJ = "#0072B2", VC = "#D55E00"),
    labels = method_labels
  ) +
  scale_shape_discrete(labels = method_labels)
p_scaled
```

## Themes {#gg-themes .plot-example .wide-code data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Use a theme to change the background, text size and legend position.

```{r}
#| label: gg-themes
#| fig-alt: "Dose-response scatterplot with a classic theme and bottom legend."
p_final <- p_scaled +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
p_final
```

## Saving a ggplot {#gg-save data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

```{r}
#| eval: false
ggsave("dose-response.png", plot = p_final,
       width = 7, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

Pass the plot object explicitly. The filename extension chooses the file format. Use PDF or SVG when you need scalable graphics.

## Choosing a plot for a new question {#wrap-up data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

A colleague has a numeric outcome for patients in three groups and wants to see spread, typical values and unusual observations.

::: {.slide-callout}
1. Which plot would you start with?
2. What does one row represent?
3. What would you map to x and y, and what would your caption say?
:::

## Data that needs reshaping {#deaths-source data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

The UK lung disease data give monthly death counts by sex. Here the group names are stored as column headings.

```{r}
#| label: deaths-wide
#| echo: false
months <- seq(as.Date("1974-01-01"), by = "month",
              length.out = length(mdeaths))
wide <- data.frame(
  month = months,
  Male = as.numeric(mdeaths),
  Female = as.numeric(fdeaths)
)
knitr::kable(head(wide, 3))
```

Which column would you map to colour to get one line per group?

## Data ready to plot {#deaths-ready data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Put each variable in its own column. Each row now gives the count for one month and one sex.

```{r}
#| label: deaths-long
#| echo: false
deaths <- data.frame(
  month = rep(months, times = 2),
  sex = rep(c("Male", "Female"),
            each = length(months)),
  count = c(as.numeric(mdeaths),
            as.numeric(fdeaths))
)
preview <- deaths[c(1:2, length(months) + (1:2)), ]
knitr::kable(preview, row.names = FALSE)
```

Map `month` to x, `count` to y and `sex` to colour.

## Plotting the reshaped data {#deaths-tidy .plot-example data-background-image="./templateassets/triangledb.svg"}

Now ggplot2 can draw a separate line for each sex group on the same date axis.

```{r}
#| label: deaths-tidy
#| fig-alt: "Monthly death counts by sex in the UK from 1974 to 1979."
ggplot(deaths,
       aes(month, count, colour = sex)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Deaths",
       colour = "Sex")
```
